michelle: Heads-up: we're seeing confusing client errors during the priority-routing canary — mix of 429s and 503s with messages like 'service unavailable'. Need to decide canonical client-facing mapping + what (if any) routing hints we expose. Thoughts?
ashok: Seen it. When high-priority traffic spills over and autoscale lags, some requests hit the dedicated pool limit -> 429, others get 503 from fallback paths. We shouldn't leak internal topology, but we need actionability.
sam: Agree on not leaking topology. Proposal: unify surface errors into clear classes and add a small machine-readable header. Example: `x-rw-error-code: capacity_unavailable` and `x-rw-retry-hint: retry-after=3` or `quota`/`fallback`. Clients can act on these without knowing routing.
michelle: Good start, but console/telemetry will lose signal if we coalesce too much. Canary health metrics depend on differentiating 'capacity throttling' vs 'fallback degradation'.
katie: :point_up: exact problem. Idea: public API returns friendly/generic messages + minimal hint header. For internal/enterprise tokens we can include `x-rw-internal-reason` with richer enums for debugging. That keeps UX tidy and opsable.
ashok: We already propagate token scopes. We can gate `x-rw-internal-reason` behind an auth flag. Public headers remain limited to `x-rw-error-code` and `x-rw-retry-hint`.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T12:08Z: Canary rollout priority-routing v2 -> 10%
sam: Also need canonical list of error_code values. My suggestion: capacity_unavailable (retryable), quota_exceeded (client action), model_unhealthy (non-retryable), fallback_degraded (retryable with fallback), invalid_request, auth_error. Keep the list small so dashboards stay stable.
michelle: SDK ergonomics matter: SDKs should map `error_code` -> exception types and default retry/backoff. Docs need a table mapping code -> user-facing message + SDK behavior. Console should show heatmap by `error_code` x `route_priority`.
katie: Telemetry schema change request: add low-cardinality tags `route_priority` (low,normal,high), `fallback_target` (only present when non-none), and `error_code`. Can we do this without exploding cardinality?
ashok: Yes — route_priority is 3 values, fallback_target only surfaced when fallback occurs, error_code bounded (~12). We'll add sampling guards to avoid high-cardinality user ids.
sam: Implementation plan:
- spec headers & canonical `error_code` list
- SDK mapping PR (translate to exceptions + retry hints)
- console backend: preserve internal metrics but expose public-friendly dashboards
- docs PR + changelog entry
Volunteers?
michelle: I'll own the spec + docs draft, will push a first pass by EOD. @ashok can you take SDK mapping? @katie can you take console mockups + alert rules? @sam can you own rollout validation + canary guardrails?
katie: On it. I'll also add an alert to trigger when `capacity_unavailable` exceeds 1% on canary for >5m.
deploy-bot: incidentbot: note: spike observed 2026-03-17T21:04Z: increased 429s in priority pool; follow-up thread created.
